meta.title: The Loop Done-Determination Packet
meta.description: What the loop slice is, why it exists, what changed under it, and the four decisions that gate dispatch

props.title: Loops End on Evidence, Not Claims
props.subtitle: The loop done-determination packet — proposed July 12, validated, re-baselined July 16, awaiting dispatch ruling

props.content: Today an agent can claim it finished and the loop believes it. This slice makes the evaluator verdict at a flow's verify gate route the loop instead: pass completes it, fail takes the already-declared retry edge up to the already-declared iteration cap, and a verdict that cannot be trusted stops everything honestly.
If you want to use a loop, this is how it works: define max_iterations, and the evals at the validate node determine if things are done or not. — operator ruling, July 4

The packet is the surviving scope of a killed earlier proposal (the eval-override island, rejected with prejudice). What survived is deliberately small: no new machinery, no new YAML vocabulary. The discovery that shaped it is that **the demo flow already declares everything the loop needs** — the runtime just ignores all of it.

This is never named *blocking*. It is done-determination: the loop's way of knowing, from evidence, that it is finished.

props.label: THE GAP
props.title: Declared but unconsumed
props.subtitle: Everything below is parsed today. None of it routes anything.

props.filename: plan-execute-verify.flow.yaml — the verify gate, as written today
props.content:
verify_gate:
  eval: "exec_result != ''"
  evaluators:
    required: [intent_conservation]
  branches:
    pass: done
    fail: plan        # retry edge — declared
  max_iterations: 3   # cap — declared
  on_timeout: done

props.title: What the runtime actually does
props.content: The gate routes on the data expression alone — one line of code picks the branch from a boolean (pass if the expression held, fail otherwise). The semantic evaluator verdict is computed and recorded on the receipt, but it never steers. The iteration cap is consumed by nothing. The retry edge has never once been taken. core/exec/src/execution/dispatch/gate.ts line 47.

props.label: THE CORE MOVE
props.title: Three verdict arms, three routes
props.subtitle: Branching composes from the discharged decision — never from the two-state boolean, because a boolean cannot represent the third state. That fence is called verdict theater, and it is the highest-risk claim in the proof design.

props.title: ✅ Decided: pass
props.content: The evaluator observed the work and it holds. Take the declared done branch. The run seals as a candidate effect — byte-identical to today's clean run.

props.title: 🔁 Decided: fail
props.content: The evaluator observed the work and it drifts. Take the declared fail branch — retry back to plan with the original inputs. Each iteration burns one attempt against the declared cap of three.

props.title: 🛑 Evaluation error
props.content: The evaluator could not observe (no samples, missing channel, companions down). No verdict is minted. Escalate immediately, seal failed with the error reason — and the attempt budget is NOT burned. An unobservable check must never masquerade as a pass or quietly eat a retry.

props.title: 🧭 Verdict-routed branching
props.content: The gate consumes the decision arms above instead of the raw boolean. The decision payload already rides every receipt and seal since the evidence cutover — this slice just makes it steer.

props.title: 🔢 Runner-enforced cap
props.content: max_iterations counted by gate-node revisits, enforced by the runner. A fail-always harness run terminates in exactly three gate visits — the declaration stops being a parsed no-op.

props.title: 🧾 Honest terminal states
props.content: Attempts exhausted → seal failed with an attempts-exhausted reason, carrying ALL iteration decision refs, and the CLI exits nonzero. Nothing that ran out of retries can look done.

props.title: 🎛️ Opt-in by existing declaration
props.content: Presence of required evaluators on the gate IS the opt-in. Zero new keys. Flows without them keep byte-identical branch behavior — pinned by replaying the recorded baseline.

props.label: ACCEPTANCE
props.title: Six things that must be true

rows.proof: Live demo run: gate visited once, branch done, seal candidate-effect — branch sequence byte-identical to the recorded baseline
Drift-injected run retries exactly three times, then seals failed with attempts-exhausted, all iteration decision refs attached, nonzero exit
Seeded evaluation error stops the run without burning an attempt
A gate without required evaluators routes from the data expression alone — byte-identical to pre-slice behavior
Fail-always run terminates in exactly the declared number of gate visits, proven from live events
The pinned trace-output contract test passes byte-untouched; no existing event field renamed or removed

props.label: RE-BASELINE · JULY 16
props.title: What moved under the packet
props.subtitle: A parallel lane landed seal-truth work for the intent-conservation gate the day before the closer look. Four findings, none fatal.

props.title: Part of the escalation story already landed
props.content: The seal-truth lane made evaluation errors typed and fail-closed: no verdict minted, seal fails, exit nonzero — live-proven. The packet's escalation acceptance shrinks to one fence: the retry budget must not be consumed.

props.title: The drift demo is now a standing CI fence
props.content: Drift currently seals failed immediately, and that exact behavior is pinned by a standing end-to-end fence. The retry slice changes what the fence pins — so the fence file must join the slice's write scope with a coordinated amendment: drift still ends failed with nonzero exit, but after three visible retries. tests/e2e/exec-drift-demo-fence.mjs

props.title: The forbidden word now exists next door
props.content: The word *blocking* appears in the eval enforcement lane — a different concept (does a failing evaluator block the receipt), landed by the parallel session. The packet's fence forbids the word for loop identifiers. Needs a scoping ruling: fence new loop names only (recommended), or schedule a rename of the enforcement word.

props.title: The core gap is untouched
props.content: The gate still routes on the boolean; the verdict still never steers; the cap is still ignored. The slice's reason to exist is fully intact, and the packet's code references are still accurate.

rows.q: Gate opts in but omits max_iterations
rows.why: A loop without a declared cap is an unbounded loop by omission; failing at load makes the author declare intent
Per-iteration failures already spell case_failed; attempts-exhausted becomes the terminal loop reason alongside it
No pause or human-hold lane yet — an honest failed seal now beats a half-built approval flow
The enforcement lane's blocking word is another team's landed concept; renaming it is their call, on their clock

props.title: Feedback into retries
props.content: V1 retries with the original node inputs. Telling the next iteration what is left and how far off it was is a later refinement, per the July 4 ruling.

props.title: The eval key collapse
props.content: Collapsing the evaluators vocabulary into the single fractal eval key belongs to the eval-authoring follow-up, which this slice unblocks. Not touched here.

props.title: The until loop lane
props.content: Orchestration's until primitive is a different loop topology with its own iteration input. This slice only touches graph-gate loops.

The packet is written and validates clean — one vertical slice, seven failure hypotheses, six falsifying fitness functions, with the drift demo itself as the live proof. The execution lane under it went fully green yesterday (exec, orchestration, daemon all passing).

Dispatch is gated on the four decisions above plus the packet amendments from the re-baseline: shrink the escalation acceptance to the budget fence, add the drift fence to the write scope, and pin the reason vocabulary. Approve those and the slice is a single bounded worker dispatch.
